releases.changelog:
VoxCPM2 now runs on audio.cpp instead of PyTorch.

- The model download is 2.96 GB instead of 4.96 GB: VoxCPM2 with its
  weights in 8-bit, as accurate and as close to the speaker as the
  original in our tests. The weights earlier versions downloaded are
  removed once the new model checks out.
- About 4.5 GB of memory instead of 7, and about a fifth faster on a CPU.
- On an Apple Silicon Mac it runs on the GPU (Metal), once a short test
  line shows that works there; otherwise on the CPU.
- A speaker's reference clip is processed once and reused for that
  speaker's next lines.
- Cancelling stops a line between two steps, and progress is reported
  step by step.
- The archives are 13 to 17 MB instead of a PyTorch bundle, and the Linux
  one runs on glibc 2.28 and newer.
- The Inference device and Weight precision settings are gone.

The add-on, audio.cpp and the VoxCPM2 weights are Apache-2.0; ggml, cJSON
and libyaml are MIT. Each archive carries THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/, with the
one change we made to audio.cpp (a step callback for cancel and progress).



**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Subtitld/addon-voxcpm/compare/v0.0.1...v26.11.1

releases.changelog:
Long audio no longer looks stuck at 20%.

Whistle used to transcribe the whole file in one go: the progress bar stopped at 20% until it finished, Cancel had to wait for the end, and long files slowed down more than their length (20 minutes took about 3 minutes). The audio is now transcribed about a minute at a time, cut at quiet moments so no word is split:

- The progress bar moves after every minute of audio.
- Cancel takes effect within a minute.
- 20 minutes of audio take about 2 minutes instead of 3, with the same words.
- With no language set, the first stretch of speech sets the language for the rest of the file.

Versions now follow Subtitld's own: year, month and the release of that month. 26.10.1 comes after 0.0.2, and Subtitld offers it as an update.

The model, the engine and the add-on are unchanged otherwise: Apache-2.0, offline, CPU only.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Subtitld/addon-whistle/compare/v0.0.2...v26.10.1

releases.changelog:
Offline English speech-to-text for Subtitld with Phonon-2 from Fermion Research (fermion-research 0.2.11).

Linux x86-64 for now. The archive runs on glibc 2.28 and newer, and was tested from the archive in clean Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 10, Fedora 44 and Arch Linux containers, with a real transcription in each. macOS and Windows builds are not done yet.

The model is not included: Phonon-2 (164 MB, CC-BY-4.0) downloads once on first use into Subtitld's shared model cache, checked against a sha256 pinned in fermion-research. English only; the Whisper (offline) add-on covers other languages. The engine runs on torch, so the download is large, about 340 MB.

The add-on is Apache-2.0. The archive contains `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES/` with the licences of everything frozen into it; `INDEX.txt` lists every shared library and the notice that covers it. The Phonon engine and transformers are Apache-2.0, torch and numpy are BSD-3-Clause, and the Python runtime and its libraries are under their own licences.

The archive also ships LGPL code, and its complete source is attached here:

- libquadmath (LGPL-2.1-or-later), in two builds, linked by the GCC Fortran runtime of numpy's and scipy's OpenBLAS: `phonon2-addon-0.0.1-libquadmath-source.tar.gz`.
- libsndfile (LGPL-2.1-or-later) from soundfile, with LAME and mpg123 (LGPL) and libFLAC, libogg, libvorbis and Opus (BSD) linked into it: `phonon2-addon-0.0.1-libsndfile-source.tar.gz`.

Each tarball's README says which build it is and how to rebuild it. The add-on's own source is `phonon2-addon-0.0.1-source.tar.gz`.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Subtitld/addon-phonon2/commits/v0.0.1

releases.changelog:
Offline text-to-speech for Subtitld with KittenML's KittenTTS 2, in 16 languages (English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hindi, Turkish, Dutch, Polish and Indonesian), at 24 kHz.

- **The speaker's own voice.** Cloned from the clip Subtitld cuts from the video, and spoken in another language too. With the subtitle text Subtitld sends with the clip, KittenTTS continues from it, which is closest to the speaker; "Clone the timbre only" leaves the words out.
- **115 built-in voices.** 50 in English, 2 to 7 in each other language.
- **About real time on a CPU.** A second of speech takes 1.1 to 1.5 seconds on an i7-13700T, with about 2.3 GB of memory. x86-64 needs AVX2, FMA and F16C; Apple Silicon works.
- **Downloads on first use.** The model, 1.66 GB, from KittenML's repository on the first line; the reference encoder, 542 MB, from this repository's ref-encoder-1 prerelease, on the first cloned line. Both are pinned and checked by sha256.

**The weights are not open source.** KittenTTS 2 is under the Stellon Labs Community License. Commercial use, dubbing for pay included, is free only below US$1,000,000 in annual revenue and in total funding, and requires registering with Stellon Labs. Use must also follow an Acceptable Use Policy that is not published, and the licence is revocable. The add-on ships none of KittenML's weights; read the licence before using it for paid work. Powered by KittenML.

Built on KittenML's C++ runtime (kitten-tts-2-cpp) with LibTorch 2.14.1, patched to end a line whose model scores go non-finite, and with the CPU flash-attention path off (it produced such lines depending on the thread count). A line that falls into silence is retried with another seed, up to three times, and the silence around each line is trimmed.

Each archive was installed in CI the way Subtitld installs add-ons, on Linux, macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows, and spoke English, Portuguese and Chinese lines and a cross-lingual clone through the add-on protocol.



**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Subtitld/addon-kittentts/compare/ref-encoder-1...v26.10.1

releases.changelog:
The first release. NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 and Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B, offline on your computer, on NVIDIA's NeMo-Speech.cpp runtime.

- **Subtitles from a file in 33 languages.** Parakeet transcribes the 25 European languages, with punctuation, numbers as digits and accurate word timing; Nemotron transcribes Arabic, Chinese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese. Long files are transcribed a minute at a time, so memory stays flat (a 12-minute film peaks at about 1.3 GB), and finished subtitles appear on the timeline as they are made.
- **Speaker labels**, when switched on in Configure: up to 8 speakers, A, B, C…, with a new subtitle at each change of speaker. The speaker model (107 MB) downloads the first time.
- **Live captions while recording**, from Nemotron, in 28 languages, with a choice of 160 ms to 1.1 s of lookahead.
- **One cue per sentence**, or subtitles of about two lines at most.

Parakeet (714 MB) and Nemotron (742 MB) each download from NVIDIA's Hugging Face repositories the first time they are needed. On a Mac with Apple Silicon the runtime uses the GPU (Metal). On x86-64 the processor needs AVX2 (Intel since 2013, AMD since 2015).

Needs Subtitld 26.10 or newer.

releases.changelog:
Choose the kind of file and the codecs, as Parabolic does. Three new
settings, beside Largest video:

- File type: MP4, MKV or WebM. Video and sound that don't fit in MP4 or WebM
  are saved as MKV, which takes any.
- Video codec: H.264 (plays everywhere), Any (the best there is, whatever
  its codec), AV1, VP9 or H.265.
- Audio codec: AAC (plays everywhere), Any or Opus.

A codec is a preference: when the website has nothing in it, the best there
is is taken. For the best a website has, choose MKV, Any, Any and the
largest video. The defaults are as before: H.264 and AAC in an MP4.
